title: Where can I watch Kiarostami’s Ten, Five Dedicated To Ozu etc Kiarostami’s Later Works

commenti.body:
Check [Cinema of the World](https://worldscinema.org/). From the 5 seconds that I searched, I found Ten (2002). I have no idea how many more of his films are there.

If you have a library card, I would check and see if you can sign up for Kanopy. It is a free streaming service with a limited number of "rentals" per month, but I see a number of Kiarostami's works in their collection right now, including *Ten*.

Do you have any old-school video rental stores in your town? Many larger cities do. I myself am fortunate to have one in my city which has a copy of *Five*. I've been saving that one for a rainy day.

I tend not to advocate pirating, but if all other recourse fails you, then let your conscience be your guide.

Probably an annoying message, but when you watch *Five*, it's really worth trying to watch the making-of documentary that's included on the DVD. *With* the supplementation of this documentary, it really makes clear a lot of what you'll find in his other films and displays his attitudes towards/ approaches to filmmaking. It might be tricky to find this without the DVD (I only ended up watching it as I found a copy in a charity shop), but I can't recommend it enough!
